To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
gap junction communication, intracellular Ca2+ and nitric oxide are critical mediators of bystander responses triggered by photodynamic injury.
gap junction communication, Ca2+, and NO play a critical role in bystander responses induced in cancer cells exposed to photodynamic therapy.
gap junction communication, Ca2+, and nitric oxide (a gas) are critical for bystander cell responses to focal phototoxicity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel therapeutic strategies for the treatment of cancer.
a novel mechanism of intercellular communication that may play a role in bystander responses triggered by ionizing and nonionzing radiation.
the development and evaluation of a new approach to cancer treatment based on photodynamic therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mechanisms of bystander effects are not yet fully understood, but the evidence that gap junctions, Ca2+, and NO signaling are involved is very strong.
gap junction channels, Ca2+ signaling and NO are critical for photodynamic bystander responses, and thus for photodynamic therapy efficacy.
the bystander effect is a complex process involving several mechanisms, which are still to be elucidated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
gap junction communication, Ca2+, and NO are key components in the bystander responses induced by photodynamic treatment.
the gap junctions are critical to mediate the propagation of the signals in the bystander effect, and that the Ca2+ and the nitric oxide are the main signals that mediate the bystander effect.
intercellular signaling, including Ca2+ wave and nitric oxide, is critical to the bystander responses triggered by photodynamic treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

bystander effects triggered in a single cell can be transmitted to neighboring cells via a complex network of signals involving gap junction communication, Ca2+-dependent NO production and other yet unidentified factors.
gap junctions are essential for the propagation of bystander responses, and that Ca2+ and nitric oxide play critical roles in the bystander response to photodynamic therapy.
the bystander effect can be modulated by pharmacological agents, which may be useful to improve cancer treatment.
